exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the shoulders, with biceps, triceps assisting.
instructions: Set up an adjustable angle bench to 90 degrees and grab two dumbbells from the rack.
Pick up the dumbbells from the floor using a neutral grip (palms facing in).
Position the end of the dumbbells on your knees and sit down on the bench.
Using a safe and controlled motion, kick your knees up one at a time in order to get each dumbbell into place.
Once the dumbbells are in place, rotate your palms so they are facing you.
Take a deep breath then press the dumbbells overhead by extending the elbows and contracting the deltoids.
As you press, rotate the dumbbells until your palms are facing forward.

exercise.name: Pigeon / Figure-4 Piriformis & Glute Stretch
exercise.description: Deep external-rotation hip stretch releasing the gluteus medius, piriformis, and deep lateral hip rotators to relieve lower-back tightness.
instructions: Cross one shin in front of your hips (or ankle over opposite knee if lying on your back).
Keep your pelvis squared and hinge forward gently from the hips while exhaling slowly.
Hold for 45-60 seconds per side without forcing knee torque.

instructions: Sit on the floor with legs extended straight in front of you and toes dorsiflexed.
Hinge forward from the hip crease keeping your chest long, reaching toward your shins or feet for 45-60 seconds.

exercise.name: Standing / Side-Lying Quadriceps Stretch
exercise.description: Lengthens the rectus femoris and vasti muscles while encouraging posterior pelvic tilt.
instructions: Stand on one leg (holding a rack for balance), grab your opposite ankle, and pull your heel toward your glute.
Keep both knees close together and lightly squeeze your glute to prevent lower-back overarching.

exercise.name: Supine Knee-to-Chest & Lumbar Decompression
exercise.description: Gentle floor decompression releasing the lumbar erectors, sacroiliac joint, and gluteus maximus after heavy squats or deadlifts.
instructions: Lie flat on your back and draw both knees (or one knee at a time) gently into your chest.
Rock slowly side-to-side across your sacrum while taking deep diaphragmatic breaths for 60 seconds.
